metadata.title: Passing For The Wrong Reason
metadata.series_position: episode 5 — the series' own closing task, run on the repo
metadata.note: cli-explainer spine, weekly work report, claude-hai channel. Episode 5. Episode 4 closed by asking the viewer what makes their green indicators go red; this commit runs that question on the repo itself and fixes two gates that could be satisfied by doing nothing. FRAMEWORK: three questions for any automated check — WHAT MAKES IT FAIL / HAS IT EVER FAILED / WHY IS IT PASSING RIGHT NOW. Falsifiability beat is the commit's own honesty: gate 5 still passes, and it passes because live mode is unimplemented, not because anyone cleared it. Every figure verified by running the old and new gate tests live — see SOURCES.md / FACTCHECK.md.

beats.role_note: series continuity — episode 4's scaffolded task, run on the repo itself
beats.narration_text: Episode four closed with a question for you: for every green indicator you trust, what makes it red, and when did it last actually go red? This week I ran that on my own repository. Gate four was the one I named on camera. Gate five, which I did not look at, turned out to be the serious one.
beats.new_visual_element: last episode's closing question, turned inward

shot.show: episode 4's viewer task above, and the two gates it turned up below
shot.visual_intent: The previous episode's question sits at the top in a bordered card. Beneath it, two gate rows resolve: GATE 4, named on camera, in ink; GATE 5, not examined, in terracotta. The second one is the beat.

beats.role_note: PROOF rubric — three questions for any automated check, shown AS A STRUCTURE before either gate is examined
beats.narration_text: Three questions for any automated check. One: what makes it fail — name the condition precisely. Two: has it ever failed — has anything actually exercised that condition? Three, and this is the one that catches you: why is it passing right now? Because a check can pass for a reason that has nothing to do with what you think it is testing.
beats.new_visual_element: the three questions, as a numbered structure

shot.show: three numbered cards: WHAT MAKES IT FAIL / HAS IT EVER FAILED / WHY IS IT PASSING NOW
shot.visual_intent: Three cards land in a row, one per narration step. The third lands in terracotta — it is the new question this episode is about, and the rubric the rest of the reel is scored against.

beats.role_note: cycle 1 ask — SPARK-LINE LAW: greeting is the spark line
beats.narration_text: So, the ask. Both gates could be satisfied by doing nothing. Give them real failure paths — conditions that a real mistake would actually trip.

shot.show: the Claude composer carrying the gate-fix prompt

props.command: claude "rewrite gates 4 and 5 so a real mistake trips them — and break-test every branch"
output: stop testing the recipe's own text
prove each branch by breaking it

beats.role_note: THE ACTUAL-CODE LAW — the OLD gate 5 test, verbatim from the previous commit
beats.narration_text: Here is the old gate five, verbatim. It passes if an approval record exists — or if the literal text, bracket to-do approve, is still sitting in the recipe. That marker is always there. It is part of the template. So the second half of that or is always true, which means the first half never had to be.

shot.show: the previous gate-5 test line from the recipe

props.title: recipes/market-sentiment-analysis-part-1.md  @ aa0c0fe
props.code:
5. Approval gate: ... require an approval record.

   Test:
     test -f logs/gate-decisions/...-approval.json
     || rg --fixed-strings "[TODO: APPROVE]" \
          "recipes/market-sentiment-analysis-part-1.md"

   # the marker is part of the template.
   # it is always present.
   # so the right-hand side is always true.
props.sparkLine: An OR whose right side never fails

beats.role_note: cycle 1 output — THE CENTREPIECE. The old test run live today, beside the folder that makes it misleading.
beats.narration_text: And it gets worse. Run that old test today, against the repository as it stands. It passes. Not because anything was approved — nothing was. It passes on the marker alone. Meanwhile the gate decisions folder now exists and holds four real records: gates one, two, three and four. Gate five is not among them. So the folder looks full, the file is absent, and the test reported a clearance that had never happened.
beats.new_visual_element: the old test passing, beside the folder that has no gate-5 record

shot.show: the old gate-5 test returning PASS beside a directory listing with gates 1-4 and no gate 5
shot.visual_intent: Left: the old test, run today, resolving to PASS in terracotta, annotated 'on the marker alone'. Right: the gate-decisions listing — gate-1, gate-2, gate-3, gate-4 in ink, and a hollow terracotta slot where gate-5 is not. Both held together; the absence is the beat.

beats.role_note: THE REVISION LAW — cycle 2, the new gate
beats.narration_text: So the new one has to read something a mistake would actually change. Not the recipe's own text. The run's own artifacts.

shot.show: the Claude composer carrying the revised gate prompt

props.command: claude "make gate 5 fail the moment a live call is recorded without an approval record naming a human"
output: scan logs/ and the raw run dirs
no approval + a live call = FAIL

beats.role_note: THE ACTUAL-CODE LAW — the NEW gate 5 test, verbatim from the recipe
beats.narration_text: Here it is. Pass if an approval record exists — or if nothing, anywhere in the run logs or the raw run directories, records a performed live call. Flip that around and it says the thing you want: the moment a live call is recorded without an approval naming a human, the gate fails.

shot.show: the current gate-5 test line from the recipe

props.title: recipes/market-sentiment-analysis-part-1.md  @ 4157a8e
props.code:
5. Approval gate: ... require an approval record.

   Test:
     test -f logs/gate-decisions/...-gate-5.json
     || ! grep -rqs '"live_call_performed": true' \
            logs/market-sentiment-analysis-part-1/ \
            data/raw/market-sentiment-analysis-part-1/runs/

   # now it reads the RUN, not the recipe.
props.sparkLine: Test the artifact, not the text

beats.role_note: cycle 2 output — the three-case break test, reproduced live
beats.narration_text: Break-tested, three cases. No live call and no approval: passes. A live call recorded with no approval: fails — and that is the path that did not exist before. A live call with an approval record on disk: passes. Three cases, three different reasons, and only one of them is a real clearance.
beats.new_visual_element: the three break-test cases and their results

shot.show: three break-test rows — the conditions and their PASS or FAIL results
shot.visual_intent: Three rows resolve one at a time: no call + no approval → PASS; live call + no approval → FAIL in terracotta, tagged 'the new path'; live call + approval → PASS. The single FAIL in the middle is what the whole commit bought.

beats.role_note: PROOF rubric — question 3 answered honestly. This is the commit's own admission and the episode's lesson.
beats.narration_text: Now the part the commit is honest about, and it is the whole lesson. The gate still passes today. And the reason it passes is not that anyone cleared it. It passes because live mode is unimplemented, so no live call is possible, so the condition that would fail it cannot occur yet. That green does not mean approved. It means not applicable. A check that cannot currently fail is not yet evidence that it works. It is only evidence that it is capable of working.
beats.new_visual_element: two different meanings of the same green

shot.show: one PASS result, and the two very different things it could mean, side by side
shot.visual_intent: A single PASS chip sits at the top. Beneath it, two panels held side by side: CLEARED — a named human signed it, in ink; NOT APPLICABLE — the failing condition cannot occur, in terracotta. An arrow from the PASS points to the terracotta one. Same green, different meaning.

beats.role_note: the ledger — the promotion, and the loops this series opened that are now closed
beats.narration_text: So the ledger. The recipe is promoted to runnable sample, version zero point two, with two to-dos open and attestation null. Runnable live is explicitly not claimed. And the things this series logged rather than hid are now closed: step three finally has a field for a wrong type, and the report's reader matches the artifact it actually serves.
beats.new_visual_element: the promotion, and the closed loops

shot.show: the recipe frontmatter beside the series loops now closed
shot.visual_intent: Left: the frontmatter as declared — status RUNNABLE-SAMPLE, recipe_version 0.2.0, todos_open 2, attestation null, with RUNNABLE-LIVE struck from consideration in terracotta. Right: two closed loops — step 3 type_errors (flagged in episode 3), report Reader (flagged in episode 4).

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW + PROOF active-task rule — question 3 turned on the viewer
beats.narration_text: Your turn, and it is question three. Take a check in your pipeline that is currently green. Paste this: tell me every reason this check could be passing, and rank them by likelihood — including the possibility that the failing condition is impossible to reach right now. A good answer separates cleared from not applicable. A bad answer tells you it is green, so it is fine.
